HomeEssentials Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeEssentials Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeEssentials' results for the Q3. Joining me on today’s call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Merchandising Officer; and Morgan Patel, Chief Stores Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeEssentials' performance for the Q3. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover six key aspects of our performance:

1. Overall Performance: We posted comparable sales growth of 2.8%, fueled by strength in hardlines and seasonal categories, while navigating softer consumer sentiment and inflation on essentials.
2. E-Commerce Growth: Digital channels reached 22% penetration, with BOPIS and curbside driving higher fulfillment margins and incremental store traffic.
3. Store Performance: Our NextGen remodels are delivering strong uplifts, with remodeled units comping well above chain averages.
4. Marketing Initiatives: Loyalty personalization and value promotions lifted repeat rates and basket sizes across regions.
5. Supply Chain Optimization: Major efficiency gains expanded margins and freed up capital for reinvestment.
6. Loyalty Program Update: Membership grew 12%, enhancing customer retention and omnichannel engagement.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide more details on our financial results.

Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q3.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.82 billion, a 2.8% increase compared to the same period last year. Gross margin was 38.2%, primarily driven by supply chain efficiencies, lower inbound freight costs, and a favorable mix shift to private labels. Operating expenses were $755 million, representing 26.8% of revenue. Net income was $210 million, or $0.95 per share. We generated $320 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently optimized at 52 days outstanding and a turnover ratio of 5.8 times, reflecting disciplined management.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

One of our standout achievements this quarter has been transformative improvements in our supply chain efficiency. In an industry where margins average just 2-4% for players like us, and disruptions such as the Red Sea crisis and port congestion have impacted competitors like Macy's and Kohl's, we've made decisive progress. These changes directly fueled a 180 basis point expansion in gross margins to 38.2%, and I'll outline the key drivers.

Starting with the metrics, inventory turnover improved 18% year-over-year to 5.8x from 4.9x across our more than 1,200 stores. Days inventory outstanding fell 14% to 52 days from 60 days, outperforming the retail benchmark of 65 days for apparel and home goods. This freed up $145 million in working capital, redirected toward store remodels and digital enhancements. Fulfillment costs dropped 11% to 4.2% of sales, thanks to a 22% reduction in inbound freight per unit. Our on-time-in-full delivery to distribution centers rose to 97.5% from 89%, matching leaders like Target, while e-commerce fulfillment accuracy reached 99.2%, supporting seamless buy online pick up in store and ship-from-store.

Driving this were efforts from our 2022 Supply Chain Resilience Initiative, bolstered by $250 million in capital expenditures over the past 18 months. We implemented AI-powered demand sensing through our Blue Yonder partnership across all 15 DCs, combining point-of-sale data, weather, and economic indicators for 92% SKU-store level accuracy, up from 78%. This reduced safety stock 25% for fast-moving private-label apparel and seasonal decor, keeping stockouts below 1.5% in holiday peaks.

Automation included goods-to-person robotics from AutoStore in Dallas, Chicago, and Los Angeles DCs, increasing pick rates 40% to 450 lines per hour. RFID covers 85% of apparel inbound, cutting cycle times 30% with Amazon-level visibility. We're piloting IBM Food Trust blockchain for grocery items, slashing recall losses 60% in tests.

Regionally, U.S. operations at 75% of our footprint benefited from Mexico nearshoring under USMCA, trimming hardlines lead times 21 days and costs 8% versus China amid tariffs. Tijuana supplies 35% of seasonal SKUs, dodging 15-20% freight hikes from Panama issues. In Canada, CN Railway intermodal boosted OTIF 15 points for our 150 stores. Europe's 15% sales share leveraged a Rotterdam hub with electric trucks, cutting emissions 28% year-over-year, appealing to 62% of eco-focused European consumers per NielsenIQ.

These efficiencies build our advantage over e-tailers. Our hybrid model offers micro-fulfillment with curbside in under 2 minutes at 90% of stores, yielding 35% higher omnichannel margins. Multi-year deals with Procter & Gamble and Unilever ensure 5-7% pricing stability. Ahead, $100 million in FY25 for warehouse management upgrades and vendor-managed inventory pilots targets 10% lower DIO and sub-4% fulfillment costs, positioning us to capture McKinsey's projected $1.5 trillion retail value by 2030.

Our supply chain is now a true profit driver.

Turning to inventory optimization strategies, we've transformed this area into a key strength. With over 150,000 SKUs across 1,200 stores, inefficiencies can erode hundreds of basis points in EBITDA, as seen with Macy's and Kohl's post-COVID excess. We've reduced DIO 28% from 72 days at end-2022 to 52 days now, lifting turnover to 6.2x from 4.8x and GMROI 15% to 185%, beating NRF's 140% benchmark.

Our approach combines data science, resilience, and execution. First, $45 million in Oracle Retail AI Merchandising Cloud integrated with SAP S/4HANA processes 15 terabytes daily from POS, app data, Google Trends, and weather, boosting seasonal forecast accuracy 22% and cutting stockouts to 4.5%. This trimmed $28 million in hardlines excess, where 60% of our $2.1 billion inventory sits.

Second, ABC-XYZ analysis with Monte Carlo cut safety stock 35% to 16%, saving 8-10% carrying costs on our credit facility. A-items like KitchenAid mixers get priority, achieving 95% in-stock in Northeast stability versus localized buffers in Sun Belt micro-DCs.

Third, omnichannel orchestration: Stores act as virtual DCs for 42% of e-comm, with 80% RFID on big-tickets enabling real-time visibility. This dropped fulfillment to $4.50 per order, lifted store traffic 11%, BOPIS to 25% digital sales. InvOptix uses IoT for automated replenishments, JIT from Whirlpool.

Fourth, VMI expanded to 35 suppliers covering 28% inventory value; P&G handles CPG via POS APIs for under 2% stockouts, earning end-caps for 14% growth. Dual-sourcing from Vietnam/Mexico cut lead times to 28 days, costs 9%.

Finally, we rationalized 12,000 SKUs toward eco-lines like bamboo bedding up 32%, hitting 91% sell-through and ESG financing savings. Targeting DIO under 48 days, unlocking $60 million cash, with 4.2x ROI on AI.

Next, on our store remodel and renovation plans, this is a high-conviction driver. With industry SSS at 2.1% per NRF, we're refreshing our footprint to compete with Amazon and Wayfair while enhancing omnichannel.

For FY25, $450 million—up 25% from FY24's $360 million, or 18% of $2.5 billion capex—targets 350 full remodels at $1.2-1.5 million each, 150 zone refreshes, 100 HVAC/ADA updates. Costs up 8% on lumber/fixtures, locked via Milliken and Steelcase contracts.

NextGen features AI analytics from Zebra/Salesforce: 40% budget on experiential zones like Maker's Corner, lifting dwell 12%, conversion 7%. 25% on tech—endless aisles via NCR, 40-inch Samsung signage for 4-6% SSS in softlines, 50% bigger BOPIS zones under 2 minutes.

20% sustainability: LED sensors cut energy 25%, low-VOC, recycled fixtures for $15-20 million IRA rebates, +15 NPS. Rest on restrooms, aisles, refreshment hubs for 9% basket growth.

Prioritizing Sunbelt (60% remodels, 25 new stores), Northeast urban (20%), Midwest/West balance. 3-year payback, 25-30% ROI, 5-8% Year 1 SSS (6.2% in 2024 cohort), 50 bps margin from shrink down 15%. +$120 million EBITDA by FY27, tying to 25% e-comm goal.

Now, regional performance variations show our playbook's strength. Q3 comps +2.8% overall on 1.8% traffic, 1.4% AUV, slight margin dip to 38.2% from promotions.

Northeast (28% sales, 340 stores): +1.5% comps, 0.9% traffic on winter/high rates; BOPIS +28%, $25 million Q3 RFID refreshes for +2.5% Q3.

Southeast (32%, 410 stores): +5.8%, 4.2% traffic from migration/tourism; margins +40 bps, $40 million capex for 60 expansions, +6-7% H2.

Midwest (22%, 280 stores): +3.9%, essentials +7.2%; VMI, geofenced campaigns, solar EV at 100 stores.

West (18%, 220 stores): -0.5% from costs/Amazon; omnichannel 32%, 8 closures, bots for +1.5% Q3.

International (5%): +4.1%, Canada +6.2%, Mexico +1.8%.

Dispersion narrows with SPI dashboard, hyper-local chains, Store 2.0 tech for 3.5-4.0% FY24 comps.

Updating key strategic initiatives under Forge Ahead—omnichannel, portfolio optimization, resilience—delivered $285 million EBITDA YTD toward $1.1 billion.

Omnichannel: BOPIS 28% digital, $145 million +35%, +18% conversion, 42% add-on buys; AI app +52% engagement, +14% AOV to $68; curbside 85% stores -22% costs; $75 million FY for 60% RFID, -30% shrink.

Stores: 45 NextGen remodels +22% comps, +16% traffic; 28 closures saved $18 million SG&A, $42 million capital; 22 new off-mall +15%; Southeast +8.2%.

Supply chain: 65% North American sourcing, turns 5.2x, DIO 68; Reno DC -17% freight; VMI <2% stockouts; Canada/Mexico hedging.

Sustainability: 25% Scope 1 cut, +9% traffic; Retail Academy cut turnover to 28%.

Finally, Q4 guidance: Revenue $2.85-2.90 billion, flat to +1.5%; SSS (1.0)% to +0.5%; gross margin 35.2-35.6%; SG&A 26.8-27.2%; op income $285-300 million; EPS $0.85-0.95.

FY24: Revenue $11.4-11.5 billion, +1.5-2.0%; comps 1.0-1.8%; gross 34.8-35.2%; op margin 7.2-7.5%; EPS $3.40-3.60, +5-10%.

Drivers: Sunbelt 2-3%, loyalty 45 million +12%, HomeForge +25%; risks port strikes, mitigated by buffers/nearshoring.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Taylor Kim, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, and after that to Morgan Patel to discuss store operations.

Taylor Kim, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Jordan. This quarter, we launched our HomeForge line, which has seen exceptional demand with 25% growth, capturing share in the $500-1,000 appliance segment from OEMs like GE as consumers prioritize value and reliability. We are excited about the potential of this new product and other upcoming launches in private-label home goods.

Morgan Patel, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, Taylor. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented NextGen remodels featuring experiential zones, digital signage, and expanded BOPIS areas, and are seeing positive results with 6.2% SSS uplifts and higher dwell times in the initial cohort.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Chen (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of supply chain disruptions like the Red Sea crisis on your sales?

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Good morning, Mike. Disruptions like the Red Sea and port congestion have pressured the industry, but our nearshoring to Mexico—now 35% of seasonal SKUs—and AI forecasting kept OTIF at 97.5%, avoiding stockouts and enabling 180 bps margin expansion. This agility helped us gain share versus peers facing 15-20% freight spikes, with freed capital supporting remodels. We're prepared for potential strikes with 90-day buffers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Lisa. For Q4, we see SSS flat to +0.5%, with traffic down mid-single digits offset by low-single digit average ticket from value tiers like Essentials Everyday and high-margin cross-sells. Ex-53rd week, toward high end. Full-year 1.0-1.8%, with Sunbelt strength and remodel momentum.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ruiz with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Ruiz (Barclays):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, David. As Jordan detailed, Blue Yonder AI hit 92% accuracy, robotics boosted picks 40%, RFID at 85%, and regional tweaks like Tijuana and Rotterdam cut costs 8-28%. This turned our chain into a moat, with 35% higher omni margins and $145 million capital release.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emma Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emma Patel (Morgan Stanley):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Great question, Emma. Our ShopSmart AI grew active households 12% to 45 million, lifting repeats 8% and omnichannel engagement. Integrated with remodels and RFID, it's driving 42% BOPIS add-ons and higher AOV, core to our personalization strategy amid value-seeking shoppers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim (Citigroup):
How are remodel plans factoring into regional comp dispersion?

Morgan Patel, Chief Stores Officer:
Thanks, Rachel. We're allocating 60% of FY25 remodels to Sunbelt power centers for 5-8% SSS, 20% Northeast urban tech upgrades to counter e-comm, balancing elsewhere. Early data shows 22% comp lifts, narrowing dispersion as traffic and conversion improve.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes today's questions.

Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.

aspect_summary.Key strategic initiatives update: Forge Ahead progress: omnichannel (BOPIS 28% digital sales, +35% growth), stores (45 NextGen remodels +22% comps, 28 closures, 22 new stores), supply chain (65% North American sourcing, 5.2x turns), sustainability (25% Scope 1 cut); $285M EBITDA YTD toward $1.1B.
aspect_summary.Store remodel and renovation plans: FY25 $450M capex (up 25%) for 350 full NextGen remodels ($1.2-1.5M each), 150 zone refreshes, 100 HVAC/ADA; features AI analytics, experiential zones, tech (endless aisles, BOPIS), sustainability (LEDs, recycled fixtures); 60% in Sunbelt, 5-8% Year 1 SSS, 25-30% ROI.
aspect_summary.Regional performance variations: Q3 comps: Southeast +5.8% (4.2% traffic, migration), Northeast +1.5% (BOPIS +28%), Midwest +3.9% (essentials +7.2%), West -0.5% (Amazon pressure, 8 closures), International +4.1% (Canada +6.2%); overall +2.8%.
